pois.name: Humpback Rocks Visitor Center
pois.desc: Northernmost VA visitor center with a reconstructed mountain farmstead and the popular steep trail to the Humpback Rocks crag.

pois.name: Humpback Rocks Trailhead
pois.desc: Trailhead for the strenuous climb to Humpback Rocks offering panoramic views of the Shenandoah Valley.

pois.name: Greenstone Overlook
pois.desc: Overlook with a short self-guiding trail through ancient greenstone (metabasalt) rock formations.

pois.name: Whetstone Ridge
pois.desc: Ridge-top stop named for the fine-grained stone once used to sharpen tools.

pois.name: Yankee Horse Ridge Overlook
pois.desc: Overlook with a reconstructed logging railroad spur and a short walk to Wigwam Falls.

pois.name: Otter Creek Campground
pois.desc: Lowest-elevation campground on the Parkway, set along Otter Creek near the James River.

pois.name: James River Visitor Center
pois.desc: Lowest point on the Parkway with a restored canal lock and footbridge over the James River.

pois.name: Thunder Ridge Overlook
pois.desc: High overlook with a short trail and sweeping views west toward the Arnold Valley.

pois.name: Apple Orchard Mountain
pois.desc: Highest point on the Parkway in Virginia (3,950 ft), topped by a former radar dome.

pois.name: Peaks of Otter Visitor Center
pois.desc: Iconic VA destination with Abbott Lake, a historic lodge, and trails up Sharp Top and Flat Top.

pois.name: Peaks of Otter Lodge
pois.desc: Lakeside lodge and restaurant at the foot of the Peaks of Otter.

pois.name: Peaks of Otter Campground
pois.desc: Wooded campground near the Peaks of Otter Visitor Center and Abbott Lake.

pois.name: Roanoke Mountain Recreation Area
pois.desc: Loop road, campground, and overlook on Roanoke Mountain just outside the city of Roanoke.

pois.name: Roanoke Mountain Campground
pois.desc: Campground convenient to Roanoke and Mill Mountain attractions.

pois.name: Smart View Recreation Area
pois.desc: Picnic area and loop trail around a restored 19th-century Trail Cabin with mountain views.

pois.name: Rocky Knob Visitor Center
pois.desc: Visitor center serving the Rocky Knob area with campground, picnic area, and Rock Castle Gorge trail.

pois.name: Rocky Knob Campground
pois.desc: Campground on a high ridge above the rugged Rock Castle Gorge.

pois.name: Mabry Mill
pois.desc: The most photographed site on the Parkway, a picturesque 1908 water-powered gristmill with a pond and living-history area.

pois.name: Groundhog Mountain
pois.desc: Picnic area with an observation tower and a display of historic split-rail fence styles.

pois.name: Blue Ridge Music Center
pois.desc: Museum and outdoor amphitheater celebrating the old-time and bluegrass music traditions of the Blue Ridge.

pois.name: Cumberland Knob
pois.desc: Birthplace of the Parkway and first NC recreation area, with picnic grounds and a loop trail.

pois.name: Doughton Park
pois.desc: One of the largest recreation areas on the Parkway with extensive meadows, trails, and wildlife viewing.

pois.name: Brinegar Cabin
pois.desc: Preserved log homestead from the early 1900s with weaving demonstrations at the north end of Doughton Park.

pois.name: Doughton Park Campground
pois.desc: Campground set in the high meadows of Doughton Park.

pois.name: E.B. Jeffress Park
pois.desc: Park with the Cascades waterfall trail and the historic Jesse Brown cabin and Cool Spring Baptist Church.

pois.name: Moses H. Cone Memorial Park
pois.desc: Historic Flat Top Manor estate with 25 miles of carriage trails, a craft center, and Bass Lake.

pois.name: Julian Price Memorial Park
pois.desc: Large recreation area centered on Price Lake with the Parkway's biggest campground and canoeing.

pois.name: Price Lake
pois.desc: Scenic 47-acre lake with a loop trail and seasonal canoe rentals beneath Grandfather Mountain.

pois.name: Julian Price Campground
pois.desc: The largest campground on the Parkway, located beside Price Lake.

pois.name: Linn Cove Viaduct
pois.desc: An engineering marvel: a 1,243-ft S-curving concrete bridge that hugs the rugged flank of Grandfather Mountain.

pois.name: Linn Cove Viaduct Visitor Center
pois.desc: Visitor center with a level trail leading beneath the famous viaduct.

pois.name: Grandfather Mountain
pois.desc: Privately run nature park (via US-221) famous for its Mile High Swinging Bridge and rugged peaks.

pois.name: Linville Falls
pois.desc: Dramatic multi-tiered waterfall plunging into the rugged Linville Gorge, with a visitor center and several viewpoint trails.

pois.name: Linville Falls Visitor Center
pois.desc: Trailhead and information center for the Linville Falls and Linville Gorge area.

pois.name: Linville Falls Campground
pois.desc: Campground along the Linville River near the falls.

pois.name: Museum of North Carolina Minerals
pois.desc: Museum at Gillespie Gap showcasing the region's rich mineral and gem deposits.

pois.name: Little Switzerland
pois.desc: Historic mountain resort community with shops and an inn just off the Parkway.

pois.name: Crabtree Falls
pois.desc: 70-ft cascade reached by a loop trail from the Crabtree Meadows recreation area.

pois.name: Crabtree Meadows Campground
pois.desc: Campground and picnic area serving the Crabtree Falls trail.

pois.name: Mount Mitchell
pois.desc: Highest peak east of the Mississippi (6,684 ft), reached by NC-128 in Mount Mitchell State Park.

pois.name: Craggy Gardens Visitor Center
pois.desc: Visitor center amid high-elevation heath balds famed for spectacular June rhododendron blooms.

pois.name: Craggy Gardens Picnic Area
pois.desc: Picnic area and trailhead into the Craggy Gardens rhododendron balds.

pois.name: Folk Art Center
pois.desc: Home of the Southern Highland Craft Guild, selling and exhibiting Appalachian crafts; also a Parkway info desk.

pois.name: Blue Ridge Parkway Visitor Center
pois.desc: The Parkway's main headquarters visitor center near Asheville with exhibits and a large interactive map.

pois.name: Mount Pisgah
pois.desc: Recreation area with a lodge, campground, and a trail to the 5,721-ft Mount Pisgah summit and its TV tower.

pois.name: Pisgah Inn
pois.desc: Mountaintop inn and restaurant with panoramic views, one of only two lodges on the Parkway.

pois.name: Mount Pisgah Campground
pois.desc: High-elevation campground near the Mount Pisgah trailhead.

pois.name: Graveyard Fields
pois.desc: Popular high-elevation valley with waterfalls, blueberries, and open meadows reached by a loop trail.

pois.name: Devil's Courthouse
pois.desc: Steep paved trail to a rocky 5,720-ft summit with sweeping views into four states.

pois.name: Richland Balsam Overlook
pois.desc: Highest point on the Parkway motor road at 6,053 ft, with a self-guiding spruce-fir forest trail nearby.

pois.name: Waterrock Knob Visitor Center
pois.desc: Highest visitor center on the Parkway, with a steep trail to the 6,292-ft Waterrock Knob summit.

pois.name: Soco Gap
pois.desc: Mountain gap where the Parkway crosses US-19 between Maggie Valley and Cherokee.

pois.name: Bluff Mountain Tunnel
pois.desc: The only tunnel in Virginia on the Parkway, about 630 ft long near Otter Creek.

pois.name: Twin Tunnels (North)
pois.desc: Northern of the paired Twin Tunnels near Buck Creek Gap.

pois.name: Twin Tunnels (South)
pois.desc: Southern of the paired Twin Tunnels near Buck Creek Gap.

pois.name: Little Switzerland Tunnel
pois.desc: Tunnel near the Little Switzerland resort community, about 542 ft long.

pois.name: Rough Ridge Tunnel
pois.desc: Shortest Parkway tunnel at about 150 ft, near the Rough Ridge area.

pois.name: Pine Mountain Tunnel
pois.desc: The longest tunnel on the Parkway at 1,434 ft, south of Asheville.

pois.name: Devil's Courthouse Tunnel
pois.desc: Tunnel bored through rock just below the Devil's Courthouse summit.

pois.name: Pinnacle Ridge Tunnel
pois.desc: Tunnel south of Waterrock Knob, about 813 ft long.
